message.content:
I have full context: contract, kernel, and metadata. I'll record the structured description model now.

Key observations to encode: FP16→FP32 log1p with 1e-6 absolute tolerance over the full legal domain; the kernel uses atanh-style range reduction with an exponent split and only a short degree-7-ish polynomial (coefficients 0.142857, 0.2, 0.33333, 1.0), with a narrow polynomial domain (mantissa split at 1.65, i.e. z roughly |z|<~0.245 only after exponent reduction... actually mantissa in [1,1.65] halved gives mantissa in [1,1.65/2... need care), truncated coefficients (0.33333 vs 1/3, 0.2 vs 1/5, 0.142857 vs 1/7), and exponent-based approach splitting ln(2) into high+low — the polynomial truncation and coefficient rounding are prime tolerance risks at the domain edges (x near -1 where u→0, and x=65504 where exponent is large). Also the case x very close to -1: u could be subnormal/zero in FP32? x is FP16 > -1, smallest value is -0.99951... u = 1+x could be as small as ~4.88e-4 (FP16 spacing above -1), fine. But correction term and large negative exponent: exponent -11, fine. Also exponent up to 16 for 65504.

function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["Compute log1p elementwise: output[i] = log(1+x[i]) in natural log, FP16 input tensor [N] (1<=N<=131072), FP32 output [N] on x.device, fresh tensor, input preserved.", "Absolute tolerance only: abs(actual - log(1+x)) <= 1e-6 with zero relative tolerance; signed zeros numerically equivalent; target defined in real arithmetic on the exact stored FP16 value.", "Full legal domain: every finite FP16 value strictly greater than -1, including both signed zeros, positive/negative subnormals, the value immediately above -1 (~-0.99951), and max FP16 65504. NaN/inf/<=-1 excluded.", "Input is an ordinary, dense, contiguous, strided CUDA torch.Tensor (contiguous views with nonzero storage offsets legal), requires_grad=False, is_inference=False, is_neg=False, is_conj=False, ordinary non-inference execution mode.", "validate_inputs() enforces the domain and is called by run(); reference() uses FP64 torch.log1p and accepts CPU inputs; make_inputs() is examples only. Single correctness verdict for the whole domain, not per-distribution.", "Frozen environment: NVIDIA T4, PyTorch 2.8.0, Triton 3.4.0."], "kernel_model": ["Triton kernel loads x as FP16, casts to FP32, computes u = 1.0 + x in FP32, and a Sterbenz-style correction correction = (x - (u-1.0)) / u using div_rn.", "Range reduction: bitcast u to uint32, extract biased exponent and implicit-1 mantissa; if mantissa > 1.65, halve mantissa and increment exponent, so log(u) = exponent*ln2 + log(mantissa).", "log(mantissa) via atanh series: z = (m-1)/(m+1), local_log = 2z * P(z^2) with polynomial 1 + (1/3 + (1/5 + (1/7)*s)*s)*s using rounded constants 0.33333, 0.2, 0.142857 — a short odd-power series truncated after z^7.", "exponent*ln(2) split into high (0.69313812256) and low (0.0000090580006145) parts; final value = high + (local_log + (low + correction)), with enable_fp_fusion=False and div_rn used to control rounding.", "run() validates inputs, allocates fresh FP32 output, launches BLOCK=256 grid with num_warps=4; masking via index < N (N passed as constexpr).", "validate_inputs checks: no inference mode, plain Tensor, strided+contiguous, no grad/inference/neg/conj flags, CUDA device, 1-D shape with N in [1,131072], FP16 dtype, all values finite and > -1."], "risk_map": ["Polynomial truncation: the series is cut at z^7 with only 3 nontrivial coefficients; after the mantissa>1.65 halving, mantissa ranges over [1, 3.3) so z can be as large as ~0.535, where the z^9 term (~z^9/9 ~ 1e-4 * scale) may far exceed the 1e-6 absolute tolerance — Skeptic should check the worst-case z (u just under a power-of-2 boundary, mantissa just under 1.65 pre-halving is fine, but u in [2, 3.3) after halving maps mantissa in [1,1.65), z_max=(1.65-1)/(1.65+1)~0.2455; but u itself in [1,1.65) has z up to ~0.245 too — verify which branch produces max |z| and the series error there).", "Rounded coefficients: 0.33333 vs 1/3 (~3.3e-6 error), 0.2 vs 1/5 (~4.4e-7? actually 0.2 = 0.200000000000000011..., but 0.33333 is off by 3.3e-6), 0.142857 vs 1/7 (~1.4e-7); coefficient error 3.3e-6 * z^3 could by itself break the 1e-6 absolute tolerance for moderate z — needs numeric evaluation.", "Large-argument case x=65504: log(65505) ~ 11.09; accuracy depends on the high/low ln2 split rounding and correction term; exponent up to 16 amplifies any ln2 constant error: check 0.69313812256 + 0.0000090580006145 vs ln2 = 0.6931471805599453 (sum = 0.69314718056..., appears consistent to ~1e-13, but FP32 rounding of high*16 etc. may matter).", "Near -1 case: x = nextafter(-1) in FP16, u ~ 4.88e-4, exponent ~ -11, mantissa branch edge; correction term and polynomial accuracy at small z; also x exactly -1+tiny where u is subnormal-adjacent is not an issue, but FP32 u = 1.0 + x loses no precision since x >= -0.99951 makes u >= 4.88e-4 normal.", "Signed zeros and subnormal x: x = -0.0 gives u = 1.0, exponent 0, mantissa 1.0, z = 0, output 0.0 — sign of output zero may be +0 vs -0 but contract says signed zeros equivalent. Positive subnormals: x tiny (~6e-8), u = 1.0 exactly in FP32, so log1p(x) ~ x is lost (output 0 vs true ~6e-8, within 1e-6 tolerance, fine).", "FP32 rounding accumulation: enable_fp_fusion=False and div_rn suggest deliberate rounding control, but tl.where/upper branch arithmetic and final summation order high + (local + (low + correction)) may still lose low bits for large exponents.", "Masking correctness: other=0.0 load for inactive lanes is safe since stores are masked; N as constexpr forces a recompile per size but is functionally fine.", "Nonzero storage offset contiguous views: Triton pointer arithmetic uses the tensor's data pointer, which for a view with storage offset points to the first stored element, so this is handled — verify no assumption of zero offset."], "open_questions": ["Worst-case |z| actually reached by the reduction: is the mantissa>1.65 halving sufficient to bound z (max appears to be (1.65-1)/(1.65+1) ~ 0.2455 on the un-halved branch and (3.3-1)/(3.3+1)? no — halved branch mantissa in [1,1.65) also gives z<0.2455; need runtime confirmation of the actual z range and the resulting truncation error vs 1e-6.", "Whether the rounded coefficient 0.33333 (vs 1/3) alone can exceed 1e-6 absolute error for reachable z values.", "Empirical max error across the full FP16 domain sweep (all 65504-ish legal values is cheap to test exhaustively) — this is the decisive probe but belongs to the Experimenter.", "Whether FP32 rounding in the final high + (...) summation for exponent up to 16 stays within tolerance."], "scope_notes": ["In scope: every finite FP16 value > -1, N in [1,131072], CUDA only via run(); reference accepts CPU. Single verdict over the entire domain, so a single failing legal value (e.g. x=65504 or the FP16 value just above -1) is decisive.", "Out of scope: NaN, inf, values <= -1, non-contiguous or non-FP16 inputs, autograd, inference-mode execution, concurrent writes — validate_inputs rejects these.", "Tolerance is absolute 1e-6 with zero relative tolerance; for large |log| values (x=65504, log~11.09) this is ~0.9 ulp at FP32 magnitude ~11, so the implementation must be near-FP32-exact at the top of the range.", "The entire FP16 legal domain is small enough (~6.4k values) for exhaustive per-value verification, which makes this case tractable for a single domain-wide verdict."], "summary": "case_166: Triton FP16->FP32 elementwise log1p with exponent-based range reduction, atanh-series polynomial, Sterbenz correction, and high/low ln(2) split; contract demands 1e-6 absolute error over all finite FP16 inputs > -1."}
